clue.text: Open bearing of former German confederates

parts.note: frank means open, candid
S, south, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Someone frankly describes the attitude of old German allies.
explanation.walkthrough: The Franks were a confederation of Germanic tribes in late Roman times.
explanation.definitionFit: The Franks were a league of early Germanic tribes, later rulers of Gaul.

clue.text: King of Italy sailed out, having cashed in

parts.note: re is Italian for king

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of sailed are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: An Italian monarch sailed away after making his fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise assets is to convert them into money.

clue.text: No basis for getting a print-out

definitions.meaning: a photographic film from which prints are made

explanation.surface: A claim that there are no grounds for a printed report.
explanation.definitionFit: A negative answer is a refusal, and a film negative is what photographic prints are made from.

clue.text: Reeds that were so broken

indicators.note: broken asks for the letters of the two words to be smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Reeds that have been smashed to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of REEDS THAT gives the answer, and the whole clue describes such reeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattered means broken into fragments.

clue.text: Dog going about in pram?

indicators.note: the dog's name goes around the next word, enclosing it

parts.note: a basset is a short-legged hound

explanation.surface: A dog is circling round a baby carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassinet is a hooded wicker cradle or baby carriage, so pram is a fair example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Gap in defences giving hope of end of engagement

parts.note: a breach is a gap broken in a wall or defences
taken as written
promise means hope, expectation

explanation.surface: A gap in the defences offers hope of the fighting ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking off a promise to marry ended an engagement and could once be sued for.

clue.text: It's no handicap to start from here

definitions.text: It's no handicap to start from here

parts.words: It's no handicap to start from here
parts.note: in golf and racing a player with zero handicap starts level, from the starting line

explanation.surface: An encouraging remark that starting here is no disadvantage.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratch player has no handicap, and starting from scratch means from the very beginning.

clue.text: Counted as less sensitive press man

parts.note: number means more numb
ED, editor, is a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A journalist reckoned as less sensitive than others.
explanation.walkthrough: Read NUMBER as 'more numb', not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbered means counted.

clue.text: Streams rushing from hill clefts

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill
rents are splits or clefts

explanation.surface: Water pours from cracks in the hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrents are violent rushing streams of water.

clue.text: But it may be a barrier to communication

definitions.text: But it may be a barrier to communication

parts.words: But it may be a barrier to communication
parts.note: the thing we talk in is the very thing that stops foreigners understanding one another

explanation.surface: A paradox: the means of talking can stop talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech is the vehicle of communication, yet different tongues block it: the language barrier.

clue.text: Preliminary application for painting text-book

definitions.meaning: an undercoat put on before the paint

explanation.surface: A beginner's manual on how to start painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A first coat sealing a surface before paint, and also an introductory reading book for learners.

clue.text: Assembly to quote return concerning food

parts.note: a diet is a formal legislative assembly

indicators.note: return asks for the quoting word to be read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A parliament quotes back its ruling on catering.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietetic describes matters of nutrition and eating.

clue.text: Goddess gives another the bird, shutting her up!

indicators.note: the goddess encloses the bird, shutting it inside her

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin
a hen is a bird

explanation.surface: A goddess jeers at a rival and silences her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives another the bird' reads as an insult, but 'another' is the definition: a second goddess, built from the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene, Greek goddess of wisdom, is a second deity after the first one in the clue.

clue.text: Very nearly finished opening the wine

indicators.note: the word is finished all but its last letter, so it is cut short

parts.note: a mouth is an opening

explanation.surface: Someone has almost polished off an opened bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermouth is a fortified wine flavoured with herbs.

clue.text: Doubly manned, like Milton's engine

definitions.meaning: Milton's Lycidas speaks of the ... engine at the door

explanation.surface: A machine operated by two, as in Milton.
explanation.definitionFit: Requiring a pair of operators, and the epithet Milton gives the mysterious engine in Lycidas.

clue.text: It's an advantage to have this on

definitions.text: It's an advantage to have this on

parts.words: It's an advantage to have this on
parts.note: the idiom 'to have the ... on someone' means to be slightly ahead of them

explanation.surface: A remark about what gives one the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge on a rival means having a slight superiority over them.

clue.text: What may be lent on foreign currency reserves

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: friends lend an ear, as in 'lend me your ears'
marks were the German currency

explanation.surface: Money set aside for loans in foreign funds.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds is to set them aside for a purpose.

clue.text: Kindness leads me to express surprise

definitions.meaning: it goes before me in the exclamation of astonishment

explanation.surface: A kind act prompts surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is the exclamation 'Goodness me!'
explanation.definitionFit: Moral virtue or benevolence, and the start of a startled exclamation.

clue.text: Prices offered are not even for the better

definitions.text: Prices offered are not even for the better

parts.words: Prices offered are not even for the better
parts.note: bookmakers quote prices to the punter (the better, one who bets), and these are not evens, so uneven

explanation.surface: A complaint that quoted prices are not fair on whoever improves things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is one who bets, and 'not even' is both odd and not at evens.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting prices are quoted as ratios, and odd numbers are those not even.

clue.text: Such were Macpherson's Gaelic poems

parts.note: James Macpherson claimed to have translated the works of an ancient Gaelic bard

explanation.surface: A remark on the style of Macpherson's Gaelic verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Macpherson's 1760s epics were attributed to the legendary bard Ossian.

clue.text: On which players may come in, depressed, exhausted

definitions.text: On which players may come in

parts.note: down means low in spirits
beat means tired out

explanation.surface: Musicians join in, though dejected and tired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' are musicians, entering on the conductor's first beat of the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The downbeat is the accented first beat of a bar, where musicians often enter.

clue.text: On the point of power one of these may help to make the right connexion

definitions.text: On the point of power one of these may help to make the right connexion

parts.words: On the point of power one of these may help to make the right connexion
parts.note: a device plugged into an electrical socket lets an otherwise unfitting plug connect

explanation.surface: Advice about making the right contacts with those near to power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point of power' is a power point, the British term for a wall socket; connexion is an old spelling of connection.
explanation.definitionFit: Plug converters fit a mismatched plug to a socket so current can flow.

clue.text: Miserable, disabled — what was his fatal sin?

definitions.text: Miserable, disabled — what was his fatal sin?

parts.words: Miserable, disabled — what was his fatal sin?
parts.note: miserable with able removed (dis-abled) leaves miser, and the deadly sin a miser has is greed for money

explanation.surface: An unhappy, crippled man asks which sin destroyed him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disabled' means take ABLE from Miserable, leaving the man himself; the answer is his sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed for wealth is one of the seven deadly sins, the one a hoarder of money commits.

clue.text: Capital state of cotton in India

definitions.meaning: the chief city of a southern Indian state, now Chennai
the former southern Indian state now called Tamil Nadu
a light patterned cotton fabric first made there

explanation.surface: The capital city of India's cotton state.
explanation.definitionFit: The old name for Chennai, of the state around it, and of the striped cotton cloth woven there.

clue.text: Lots of applause — no tax is on make-up!

parts.note: O, zero, means none
VAT is value added tax

indicators.note: make-up asks for the letters to be made up again in a new order

explanation.surface: Cheers because cosmetics are exempt from tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like cosmetics but signals an anagram of O, VAT, IS, ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovations are bursts of enthusiastic clapping.

clue.text: So smoky, old Dunedin

definitions.meaning: a Scots word for full of smoke
Auld ... is the old nickname of Edinburgh, whose Gaelic name is Dunedin

explanation.surface: An observation that old Edinburgh was very smoky.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots for smoky, and the second half of Auld Reekie, the nickname for Edinburgh.

clue.text: Having deep recesses as ordered

definitions.meaning: to indent for goods is to order them formally

explanation.surface: A coastline described as deeply cut, as requested.
explanation.definitionFit: A jagged coastline has deep inlets, and an indent is also an official requisition for stores.

clue.text: Sir Patrick sue about such an account?

indicators.note: about places the word sue around the ballad hero's surname

parts.note: taken as written
Sir Patrick Spens is the hero of a Scottish ballad

explanation.surface: A Sir Patrick takes legal action over some statement.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Patrick Spens, of the old Scottish ballad, drowns at sea; his surname goes inside SUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspense account is a ledger entry holding sums until their proper place is known.

clue.text: French subject entitled to Join women's service for the money

parts.note: a duc is a French duke, a titled subject
ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the British women's army corps

explanation.surface: A Frenchman joins the women's army for pay.
explanation.walkthrough: The ATS was the Second World War women's branch of the British army.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducats were gold coins used across Europe, so cash or money.
